1327	    match args.loss_type:
1328	        case "policy_loss":
1329	            func = policy_loss_function
1330	        case "value_loss":
1331	            func = value_loss_function
1332	        case "sft_loss":
1333	            func = sft_loss_function
1334	        case "custom_loss":
1335	            func = load_function(args.custom_loss_function_path)
1336	        case _:
1337	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {args.loss_type}")
1338	
1339	    if args.recompute_loss_function:
1340	        loss, log = checkpoint(func, args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean, use_reentrant=False)
1341	    else:
1342	        loss, log = func(args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean)

1345	    # padding). Without this, gradient doesn't flow through their attention path, so
1346	    # the CP gather's backward (reduce-scatter) is not called, deadlocking other CP

1365	        (num_tokens if args.calculate_per_token_loss else torch.tensor(1, device=logits.device)),

1373	            # substitute the constant directly, instead of routing it through
1374	            # per-mb fractions.
1375	            "values": torch.tensor(
1376	                [
1377	                    num_tokens if args.calculate_per_token_loss else 0,
1378	                ]
1379	                + list(log.values()),

127	def reduce_train_step_metrics(
128	    losses_reduced: list[dict],
129	    *,
130	    calculate_per_token_loss: bool,
131	    step_global_batch_size: int,
132	    cp_size: int,
133	    dp_with_cp_group,
134	) -> dict[str, float]:
135	    """Aggregate per-mb log dicts into the dict ``train_one_step`` reports.
136	
137	    Pipeline (1:1 with what the train loop used to do inline):
138	      1. Sum each metric's per-mb ``values`` tensor locally on this rank.
139	      2. All-reduce across the DP*CP group (``dp_with_cp_group``).
140	      3. Apply the per-mode divisor / cp_factor:
141	         - per-token-loss: divisor = ``values[0]`` = all-reduced ``num_tokens``,
142	           CP-inflated by ``cp_size`` because every CP rank computes the same
143	           num_tokens off the FULL (not chunked) masks; the
144	           ``cp_factor = cp_size`` multiplier cancels that inflation, leaving
145	           the genuine per-token average.
146	         - per-rollout-mean: divisor = constant ``step_global_batch_size`` from
147	           the rollout side, never all-reduced, so no CP inflation to cancel
148	           and ``cp_factor = 1``.
149	
150	    Tests pass a mock ``dp_with_cp_group`` and monkeypatch ``dist.all_reduce``
151	    to a no-op, then pre-aggregate virtual ranks themselves — this exercises
152	    the same call shape as production while staying single-process.
153	    """
154	    keys = losses_reduced[0]["keys"]
155	    values = None
156	    for x in losses_reduced:
157	        values = x["values"] if values is None else values + x["values"]
158	    assert len(keys) + 1 == values.numel()
159	    dist.all_reduce(values, group=dp_with_cp_group)
160	    values = values.tolist()
161	
162	    if calculate_per_token_loss:
163	        num_samples_or_tokens = values[0]
164	        cp_factor = cp_size
165	    else:
166	        num_samples_or_tokens = step_global_batch_size
167	        cp_factor = 1
168	    return {key: value * cp_factor / num_samples_or_tokens for key, value in zip(keys, values[1:], strict=False)}

173	    *,
174	    cp_size: int,
175	    num_rollouts_in_rollout: int,
176	    dp_size: int,

183	    cp_size`` ranks, and each rank emits the same ``count``, so the totals

193	    count = num_rollouts_in_rollout / dp_size

197	def gather_and_reduce_log_dict(
198	    log_dict: dict,
199	    *,
200	    dp_size: int,
201	    dp_src_rank: int,
202	    dp_group,
203	) -> dict | None:
204	    """``dist.gather_object`` per-rank log_dicts + per-key reduction.
205	
206	    Per key in the gathered dicts:
207	      - ``(sum, count)`` tuple → ``Σsum / Σcount`` (per-rollout-mean shape;
208	        pair with :func:`rollout_log_metric_contribution`).
209	      - plain value → ``Σ / dp_size`` (legacy mean-across-ranks; the only
210	        correct answer when ranks hold the same data).
211	
212	    Returns the reduced dict on ``dp_src_rank``, ``None`` elsewhere. The
213	    caller adds whatever metric-name prefix / wandb plumbing it wants —
214	    this helper stays free of side effects so CPU multi-process unit tests
215	    can drive it directly with real ``torch.distributed``.
216	    """
217	    if dist.get_rank() == dp_src_rank:
218	        gathered = [None] * dp_size
219	        dist.gather_object(log_dict, gathered, dst=dp_src_rank, group=dp_group)
220	        reduced: dict = {}
221	        for key in log_dict:
222	            values = [d[key] for d in gathered]
223	            first = values[0]
224	            if isinstance(first, tuple) and len(first) == 2:
225	                total_sum = sum(v[0] for v in values)
226	                total_count = sum(v[1] for v in values)
227	                reduced[key] = total_sum / total_count if total_count else 0.0
228	            else:
229	                reduced[key] = sum(values) / dp_size
230	        return reduced
231	    dist.gather_object(log_dict, None, dst=dp_src_rank, group=dp_group)
232	    return None

235	def all_gather_with_cp(tensor: torch.Tensor, total_length: int, response_length: int) -> torch.Tensor:
236	    """
237	    Gather tensors across all ranks in the context parallel group.
238	    The first dimension of the output tensor will be the `response_length`.
239	    """
240	    cp_group = mpu.get_context_parallel_group()
241	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
242	
243	    if cp_size == 1:
244	        return tensor
245	
246	    _, _, logits_offset, _ = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(total_length, response_length)
247	
248	    prompt_length = total_length - response_length
249	
250	    chunk_0 = tensor[: logits_offset[0][1] - logits_offset[0][0]]
251	    chunk_1 = tensor[logits_offset[0][1] - logits_offset[0][0] :]
252	    assert chunk_1.shape[0] == logits_offset[1][1] - logits_offset[1][0]
253	
254	    def zero(len: int) -> torch.Tensor:
255	        return torch.zeros(
256	            [len] + list(tensor.shape[1:]),
257	            dtype=tensor.dtype,
258	            device=tensor.device,
259	            requires_grad=True,
260	        )
261	
262	    # logprob should be within the range of [prompt_length - 1, total_length - 1]
263	    if chunk_0.shape[0] == 0 and chunk_1.shape[0] == 0:
264	        # all empty
265	        full_tensor = zero(response_length)
266	    elif chunk_0.shape[0] != 0 and chunk_1.shape[0] == 0:
267	        # only first chunk
268	        left = zero(logits_offset[0][0] - (prompt_length - 1))
269	        right = zero(total_length - 1 - logits_offset[0][1])
270	        full_tensor = torch.cat([left, chunk_0, right], dim=0)
271	    elif chunk_0.shape[0] == 0 and chunk_1.shape[0] != 0:
272	        # only second chunk
273	        left = zero(logits_offset[1][0] - (prompt_length - 1))
274	        right = zero(total_length - 1 - logits_offset[1][1])
275	        full_tensor = torch.cat([left, chunk_1, right], dim=0)
276	    else:
277	        left = zero(logits_offset[0][0] - (prompt_length - 1))
278	        mid = zero(logits_offset[1][0] - logits_offset[0][1])
279	        right = zero(total_length - 1 - logits_offset[1][1])
280	        full_tensor = torch.cat([left, chunk_0, mid, chunk_1, right], dim=0)
281	
282	    assert full_tensor.shape[0] == response_length, f"Expected {response_length}, got {full_tensor.shape}"
283	    full_tensor = dist.nn.all_reduce(full_tensor, group=cp_group)
284	    return full_tensor

287	def slice_with_cp(
288	    tokens: torch.Tensor,
289	    pad_value: tuple[int, float, Callable],
290	) -> torch.Tensor:
291	    cp_rank = mpu.get_context_parallel_rank()
292	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
293	
294	    def pad_tokens(tokens, pad):
295	        if isinstance(pad_value, Callable):
296	            pad_func = pad_value
297	            tokens = pad_func(tokens, pad)
298	        else:
299	            # pad on the first dimension
300	            pad_tuple = (0, 0) * (tokens.dim() - 1) + (0, pad)
301	            tokens = F.pad(tokens, pad_tuple, value=pad_value)
302	        return tokens
303	
304	    if cp_size == 1:
305	        return tokens
306	
307	    token_len = len(tokens)
308	    chunk_size = (token_len + 2 * cp_size - 1) // (2 * cp_size)
309	
310	    # pad
311	    pad = 2 * cp_size * chunk_size - token_len
312	    tokens = pad_tokens(tokens, pad)
313	
314	    # get 2 chunk for thd cp
315	    start_1, end_1 = chunk_size * cp_rank, chunk_size * (cp_rank + 1)
316	    start_2, end_2 = chunk_size * (2 * cp_size - cp_rank - 1), chunk_size * (2 * cp_size - cp_rank)
317	    return torch.cat([tokens[start_1:end_1], tokens[start_2:end_2]])

The frozen slice looks **operationally successful and clearly improved on held-out exact match, but not unambiguously healthy**: learning is supported, while extreme response shortening, a late plateau, sparse GRPO contrast, and missing optimizer diagnostics limit a stronger conclusion.

- **Held-out performance improved substantially, then mostly plateaued.** `eval/nq_test` rose from **0.048 at step 0** to **0.1587 at step 69**, peaked at **0.1657 at step 189**, and ended at **0.1647 at step 199**—a final gain of **11.67 percentage points / 3.43× baseline** (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log:5-12,24-25`; `outputs/metrics.json:25-172`). About **95% of the final absolute gain occurred by step 69**; steps 79–199 fluctuated roughly between 0.148 and 0.1657 rather than showing continued clear growth. This supports real learning, not sustained improvement throughout the run.

- **Raw rollout reward corroborates learning better than centered GRPO means.** Across the 200 records in `output.log`, mean `rollout/raw_reward` increased from **0.0670 over steps 0–19** to **0.1975 over steps 180–199**, although minibatches remained noisy. It was comparatively flat around **0.154** during steps 60–119 before rising again (`wandb/offline-run-20260821_033838-wi4fh8cz/files/output.log:6-423`; representative initial/final records at `:6` and `:405-423`). Thus, training reward and held-out score both improve, but their later trends are not identical.

- **The near-zero `rollout/rewards` and `rollout/advantages` means do not establish near-zero per-sample rewards or gradients.** They are approximately **10^-9** aggregates with both positive and negative values, consistent with centered/normalized logging; the effective config enables GRPO, reward normalization, and GRPO standard-deviation normalization (`config.yaml:2545-2547,2575-2583`). These batch means reveal neither per-sample standard deviations nor gradient magnitudes. Conversely, they also cannot prove that updates were numerically well-scaled.

- **There is evidence of sparse within-group learning contrast.** With 32 prompts and 8 samples/prompt configured (`config.yaml:2435-2440`), `rollout/zero_std/count_0` is commonly around **18–26**; its 20-step mean is **22.55 at both the beginning and end**. Late records also contain `zero_std/count_1.0`; for example, step 199 logs 26 zero-reward and 5 one-reward zero-STD groups (`output.log:422-423`). If these keys denote what their names indicate, many groups provide no within-group contrast, although not necessarily all groups. This is an optimization weakness, not evidence that every advantage is zero.

- **Truncation improved dramatically, alongside extreme response shortening.** Held-out truncation fell from **38.13% to 0%**, while mean response length fell from **1568.6 to 9.76 tokens**; rollout truncation similarly fell from **40.63%** to mostly zero and length from **1751.5** to roughly **10 tokens** (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log:5,25,27-46`). The final held-out median is **9 tokens**, with repetition fraction zero (`output.log:424`). Eliminating truncation is healthy, and short answers can suit NQ exact match, but this is also a substantial behavioral collapse/shortcut risk. Without generations or search/tool-use traces, the logs cannot distinguish appropriate concise answering from abandonment of retrieval or reward hacking.

- **Runtime evidence does not show a training crash in the frozen slice.** All **200 rollout records and 21 evaluations** are present; evaluations span **03:45:55–05:22:52**, about **1 h 37 m** (`output.log:4-424`). Mean logged rollout-generation time fell from **20.37 s** in steps 0–19 to **2.87 s** in steps 180–199, largely alongside shorter generations. The broader job later transitioned to `Killing` because of **USER_ACTION / StopRequested**, not an observed training failure (`experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log:364-367`). Repeated **403 InvalidAccessKeyId** errors concern Teleport session-upload infrastructure, not demonstrated RL numerical failure (`experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log:1960-1968`).

**What cannot be concluded:** these are reconstructed historical W&B metrics, not an independent fresh evaluation (`outputs/metrics.json:4,20-24`; `outputs/historical_eval_trace.log:1-3`). Evaluation used 3,000 test prompts with one sample at temperature 1.0 (`config.yaml:4382-4400`), with no repeated-seed uncertainty estimates or separate untouched final test. The log supplies no grad-norm, policy-loss, clip-fraction, entropy, parameter-update, or meaningful KL trajectory—indeed `rollout/kl` is logged as zero throughout—so optimizer stability and KL regularization cannot be verified. Finally, `run_once.ok` and the frozen step-200 cutoff describe snapshot/receipt success, not successful completion of the full original 3,000-rollout run (`outputs/metrics.json:4-10`).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The original user request was:

“Read-only forensic review of /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace. Do not modify any files, run training, or use network. Inspect effective launch/config (especially examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh), train.py, data processing, reward implementation, rollout/truncation/optimization code as relevant. Identify concrete implementation/config root causes that could explain observed experiment behavior, but do not assume causality. Return exact file:line references and explain effective values and causal mechanisms. Search breadth: very thorough. Leave log/metric numerical analysis to the main agent unless needed to resolve code semantics.”

Additional governing constraints:
- Read-only exploration only.
- No file creation, modification, deletion, moving, copying, temporary files, or state-changing commands.
- No training or network access.
- Return findings directly in the response, with absolute paths.
- Do not write report/summary/findings Markdown files.
- Do not claim causality solely because a suspicious implementation was found.
- Numerical log/metric analysis belongs to the main agent except where needed to understand code semantics.

The latest user request superseded active investigation with a compaction request: respond with TEXT ONLY, no tools, and provide an analysis block followed by a detailed summary block.

2. Key Technical Concepts:

- Search-R1 multi-turn retrieval-augmented generation.
- Qwen2.5-3B with Qwen chat-template formatting.
- slime training framework using Ray, SGLang, and Megatron.
- GRPO/PPO policy optimization.
- Per-prompt reward centering and standard-deviation normalization.
- Exact-match answer reward and nominal format/retrieval shaping.
- Tool/environment-token loss masking.
- Per-request versus whole-trajectory generation limits.
- SGLang finish reasons: stop, length, abort.
- Sample statuses: COMPLETED, TRUNCATED, ABORTED.
- Fixed reference-model KL loss versus reward-level KL.
- Dynamic sampling filters and zero-variance GRPO groups.
- Stochastic evaluation inherited from rollout sampling defaults.
- Historical W&B configuration versus current launch-script configuration.
- Local dense retrieval using E5 and FAISS.
- Asynchronous retrieval concurrency and timeout behavior.

3. Files and Code Sections:

A. /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace/examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh

Purpose: Current effective launch recipe.

Important current values:
- Lines 83-94: DATA_DIR and MODEL_DIR default to $PWD; dataset and model paths are therefore working-directory dependent.
- Lines 111-117: HF checkpoint, reference torch_dist checkpoint, save path, save interval 10.
- Lines 227-249:
  - prompt-data=$TRAIN_DATA
  - input-key=prompt
  - label-key=reward_model
  - apply-chat-template enabled
  - rollout-shuffle enabled

- Lines 268-279:
  - advantage-estimator=grpo
  - use-kl-loss enabled
  - kl-loss-coef=0.001
  - kl-loss-type=low_var_kl
  - entropy-coef=0
  - eps-clip=0.2
  - eps-clip-high=0.28
  - TIS commented out
- Lines 281-288:
  - Adam
  - lr=1e-6
  - constant LR
  - weight decay=0.01
  - beta1=0.9
  - beta2=0.98
- Lines 300-303: two GPUs per SGLang engine, static memory fraction 0.7.
- Lines 316-323:
  - custom generator=generate_with_search.generate
  - custom reward=generate_with_search.reward_func
- Lines 337-353: actual train.py Ray job submission.
- No dynamic sampling filter or rollout sample filter is configured.

The 32 prompts × 8 samples = 256 generated samples, matching global-batch-size=256.

B. /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace/train.py

Purpose: Top-level training/evaluation/save order.

- Lines 49-53: evaluation occurs before training at rollout 0 unless skipped; then generation occurs.
- Lines 61-69: actor-only training path because critic is not configured.
- Lines 71-80: periodic saving and optional rollout dataset-state saving.
- Line 85: updated actor weights are pushed to rollout after every training iteration.
- Lines 90-91: periodic evaluation after training.
- Lines 97-99: parse_args then train(args).

C. /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace/examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py

This is the highest-priority implementation file.

Configuration:
- Lines 14-38:
  - max_turns=8
  - topk=3
  - search_concurrency=256
  - local backend
  - local URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve
  - return_logprob=True
  - format_score=0.2

Retrieval-body omission:
- Lines 44-56 define _passages2string.
- Lines 51-54 read the document contents and compute both title and text.
- Line 54 appends only:
  `format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"`
- The computed `text` is never appended.
- Mechanism: a search observation contains document titles but no passage bodies, so the policy cannot use the retrieved prose even though retrieval succeeded.

Stop behavior:
- Lines 164-177 add </search> and </answer> to SGLang stop strings.
- Lines 93-98 explain why string postprocessing is disabled when log probabilities are requested.
- This avoids post-answer/post-search junk while retaining closing tags through no_stop_trim.

Generation loop and token accounting:
- Lines 145-160 initialize prompt/token/mask state.
- Lines 179-188 issue one request per turn using the same sampling_params.
- There is no reduction of max_new_tokens by accumulated response_length.
- Lines 217-226 append model-generated tokens as trainable.
- Line 219 also adds ones to a separate local `loss_mask`.
- Lines 232-233 break when the current request finishes with length.
- Lines 235-244 execute the action and append observation tokens.
- Line 243 adds ones for observation tokens to the local mask:
  `loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)`
- Line 244 correctly calls:
  `sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)`
- However, line 259 finally overwrites the correct internal mask:
  `sample.loss_mask = loss_mask`
- Mechanism: the final mask contains ones for generated tokens and observation tokens, undoing trainable=False. Retrieved titles, information tags, and invalid-action instructions can therefore enter policy and KL losses.

Log probabilities:
- Lines 246-248 append dummy zero rollout log probabilities for observation tokens.
- Lines 262-264 store rollout log probabilities.
- In the saved effective configuration, use_rollout_logprobs=False and use_tis=False, so these dummy zeros are not the normal PPO old-policy log probabilities. The mask overwrite remains relevant independently.

Final status:
- Lines 266-272 derive status only from the last output’s finish reason:
  - length → TRUNCATED
  - abort → ABORTED
  - stop → COMPLETED
- Mechanism: if all eight turns are exhausted without an answer but the last request ends with stop, the sample can be marked COMPLETED despite lacking a final answer.

Reward:
- Lines 277-293 define reward_func.
- Lines 287-290 call compute_score_em on `sample.prompt + sample.response`, using `sample.label["ground_truth"]`, and pass `format_score=0.2`.
- There is no status check, so truncated samples are scored and returned to training like other samples.

Action/error behavior:
- Lines 111-121 select the first complete search/answer block.
- Lines 124-142 wrap search results in information tags or produce an invalid-action instruction.
- Lines 137-139 show that the invalid-action instruction becomes an observation; due to the mask overwrite, it is trainable.

D. /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace/examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py

Purpose: Exact-match and sequence-format reward.

Answer normalization and EM:
- Lines 21-48 lowercase, remove punctuation/articles, normalize whitespace, and compare against any golden answer.

Format validator:
- Lines 51-123 require an assistant marker and a strict state machine involving think/search/information/answer tags.
- Content outside allowed tagged regions or trailing content can make the sequence invalid.

Answer extraction:
- Lines 126-138:
  - Find all `<answer>(.*?)</answer>` matches.
  - Return None for zero or one total match.
  - Return the final match only when at least two total matches exist.
- This must be interpreted together with the dataset prompt and reward_func. The prompt contains an example answer, and scoring uses prompt+response. Therefore:
  - no generated answer → only the prompt example → None;
  - one generated answer → two total matches → generated answer extracted.
- The generator stops at the first generated </answer>, making one generated answer the normal case.

Retrieval correctness:
- Lines 141-153 check whether any normalized golden answer is a substring of any normalized information block.
- This is only used when the sequence is valid, and its reward weight is effectively zero.

Reward parameters and effective score:
- Lines 156-165 define:
  - structure_format_score=0
  - final_format_score=0
  - retrieval_score=0
  - format_score=0
  - score=1.0
- `format_score` is never used in the function body.
- Lines 175-208 implement the scoring branches.
- With reward_func passing only format_score=0.2, the effective outcomes are:
  - no extracted answer, valid or invalid → 0;
  - correct extracted answer, valid → 1;
  - correct extracted answer, invalid → 1, because score-structure_format_score = 1-0;
  - incorrect extracted answer, valid → 0;
  - incorrect extracted answer, invalid → 0.
- The comments mentioning 0.2/0.3/0.8/0.1 do not reflect the effective arguments.
- Mechanism: there is no effective positive format or retrieval shaping and no format penalty for a correct answer. The configured 0.2 value is misleading.

E. Dataset construction

Files:

- /user/user1/harbor-runs/180eb6db2085/workspace/Search-R1/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py

51	def is_valid_sequence(text):
52	    # Find the position of "<|im_start|>assistant" with potential whitespace
53	    assistant_pattern = r"<\|im_start\|>assistant\s*"
54	    assistant_match = re.search(assistant_pattern, text)
55	
56	    if not assistant_match:
57	        return False, "Missing assistant marker"
58	
59	    # Extract the content after the assistant marker
60	    start_pos = assistant_match.end()
61	    content = text[start_pos:]
62	
63	    # Check for balanced tags
64	    tags_to_check = ["think", "search", "information", "answer"]
65	    for tag in tags_to_check:
66	        opening_count = len(re.findall(f"<{tag}>", content))
67	        closing_count = len(re.findall(f"</{tag}>", content))
68	        if opening_count != closing_count:
69	            return False, f"Mismatch in {tag} tags: {opening_count} opening vs {closing_count} closing tags"
70	
71	    # Now check for proper sequence pattern and no extraneous content
72	
73	    # 1. First split the content by any tags we recognize
74	    split_pattern = r"(</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>)"
75	    parts = re.split(split_pattern, content)
76	
77	    # 2. Keep track of the current position in the expected sequence
78	    state = "start"  # start -> think -> search -> information -> think -> ... -> answer -> end
79	
80	    # 3. Check each part
81	    for _i, part in enumerate(parts):
82	        # Skip empty parts
83	        if not part.strip():
84	            continue
85	
86	        # Check if this is a tag
87	        if re.match(r"</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>", part):
88	            # This is a tag, check if it's valid in the current state
89	            if part == "<think>" and state in ["start", "information"]:
90	                state = "in_think"
91	            elif part == "</think>" and state == "in_think":
92	                state = "after_think"
93	            elif part == "<search>" and state == "after_think":
94	                state = "in_search"
95	            elif part == "</search>" and state == "in_search":
96	                state = "after_search"
97	            elif part == "<information>" and state == "after_search":

99	            elif part == "</information>" and state == "in_information":

103	            elif part == "</answer>" and state == "in_answer":

105	            else:

107	        else:

109	            if state in ["in_think", "in_search", "in_information", "in_answer"]:

5	from slime.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger, finish_tracking, init_tracking

9	def train(args):
10	    configure_logger()
11	    release_train = args.release_train
12	
13	    # allocate the GPUs
14	    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
15	    init_tracking(args)
16	
17	    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
18	    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
19	    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])
20	
21	    actor_model, critic_model = create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)
22	
23	    if args.offload_rollout and not release_train:
24	        ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote())
25	
26	    # Always push actor weights to rollout once weights are loaded.
27	    actor_model.update_weights()
28	
29	    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
30	        ray.get(rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="compare"))
31	
32	    if args.offload_rollout:
33	        ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote())
34	
35	    # special case for eval-only
36	    if args.num_rollout == 0 and args.eval_interval is not None:
37	        ray.get(rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id=0))
38	
39	    def offload_train(actor_trains_this_step):
40	        # Each model auto-offloads after train() when offload_train is set,
41	        # so we only need clear_memory for the non-offload case.
42	        if not args.offload_train:
43	            if not args.use_critic or actor_trains_this_step:
44	                actor_model.clear_memory()
45	            else:
46	                critic_model.clear_memory()
47	
48	    # train loop.
49	    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
50	        if args.eval_interval is not None and rollout_id == 0 and not args.skip_eval_before_train:
51	            ray.get(rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id))
52	
53	        rollout_data_ref = ray.get(rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id))
54	
55	        if args.offload_rollout:
56	            ray.get(rollout_manager.offload.remote())
57	
58	        if release_train:
59	            actor_model.create()
60	
61	        actor_trains = (not args.use_critic) or rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps
62	        if args.use_critic:
63	            value_refs = critic_model.async_train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref)
64	            if actor_trains:
65	                ray.get(actor_model.async_train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref, external_data=value_refs))
66	            else:
67	                ray.get(value_refs)
68	        else:
69	            ray.get(actor_model.async_train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref))
70	
71	        if release_train or should_run_periodic_action(
72	            rollout_id, args.save_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch, args.num_rollout
73	        ):
74	            force_sync = release_train or rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1
75	            if actor_trains:
76	                actor_model.save_model(rollout_id, force_sync=force_sync)
77	            if args.use_critic:
78	                critic_model.save_model(rollout_id, force_sync=force_sync)
79	            if args.rollout_global_dataset:
80	                ray.get(rollout_manager.save.remote(rollout_id))
81	
82	        offload_train(actor_trains)
83	        if args.offload_rollout and not release_train:
84	            ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote())
85	        actor_model.update_weights()
86	
87	        if args.offload_rollout:
88	            ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote())
89	
90	        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.eval_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch):
91	            ray.get(rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id))
92	
93	    ray.get(rollout_manager.dispose.remote())
94	    finish_tracking(args)
95	
96	
97	if __name__ == "__main__":
98	    args = parse_args()
99	    train(args)

#!/bin/bash

# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
kill_python_except_retriever() {
   local keep pid
   keep=" $(pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do
      case "$keep" in
         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;
      esac
   done
}

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever

set -ex

# The rollout runs up to search_concurrency (256) concurrent aiohttp requests to
# the local retrieval server, on top of sglang/ray file descriptors. The default
# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with
# "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files". Raise it as high as the hard limit
# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.
ulimit -n "$(ulimit -Hn)"

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Online W&B initialization is unreliable from this devspace and a timeout
# kills the RolloutManager actor. Default to local logging; callers can opt in
# with WANDB_MODE=online once network access is stable.
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}

# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the
# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0

# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every
# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that
# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's "ray job submit" then routes its
# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a
# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend
# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all
# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the
# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;
# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.
NODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true
if [ -z "${NODE_IP:-}" ]; then
   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true
fi
case "${NODE_IP:-}" in
   *.*.*.*)
      PREFIX16=$(echo "$NODE_IP" | awk -F. '{print $1"."$2".0.0/16"}')
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
   *)
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
esac

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/search-r1)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}
bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/prepare_data.sh"

DATASET_DIR=${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet}
TEST_DATA=${TEST_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet}

# Model checkpoints under MODEL_DIR: the HF checkpoint and its mcore
# (torch_dist) conversion used as the reference weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save-interval 10
)

# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------
# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to
# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.
#
# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths
# that run this script are able to start it themselves:
#
#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around
#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and
#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a
#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is
#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just
#     hangs until the stage timeout;
#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no
#     GPU at all;
#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,
#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.
#
# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs
# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. It also has to happen before
# `ray start` below, so that sglang sizes its engines against the memory the
# faiss shards already hold (see the SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK
# note above).
#
# An already-listening server is reused rather than restarted: loading the 60GiB
# index takes minutes, which is the same reason kill_python_except_retriever at
# the top of this file spares it across reruns.
RETRIEVAL_PORT=${RETRIEVAL_PORT:-8000}
RETRIEVAL_LOG=${RETRIEVAL_LOG:-$SLIME_DIR/retrieval_server.log}
# 30 minutes. A *cold* start also has to turn the 14GB corpus into datasets'
# arrow cache, which is the slow half; environment/prepare.sh warms that cache
# so the usual start is a few minutes. The guard has to cover the cold case
# anyway -- nothing guarantees prepare ran.
RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}

# really does mean "ready" -- no separate health request needed.

# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has
# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as "already dead" would abort a start
# that is fine.

   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of

   # actually hold.

14	SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
15	    # ============== General Configuration ==============
16	    "max_turns": 8,
17	    "topk": 3,
18	    "search_concurrency": 256,
19	    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
20	    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"
21	    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
22	    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
23	    "local": {
24	        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
25	        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
26	    },

29	    "google": {

31	        "snippet_only": True,  # Set to True to only return snippets
32	        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
33	    },

35	    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities for TIS metrics

41	SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_concurrency"])

44	def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
45	    """
46	    Convert retrieval results to a formatted string.
47	    This function works with both google_search and local_search results.
48	    """
49	    format_reference = ""
50	    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
51	        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
52	        title = content.split("\n")[0]
53	        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
54	        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"
55	
56	    return format_reference

59	async def search(query: str) -> str:
60	    """
61	    Perform search using either local search engine or Google search.
62	    The search backend is determined by SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"].
63	    """
64	    backend = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"]
65	
66	    if backend == "local":
67	        from local_search_server import local_search
68	
69	        local_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["local"]
70	        result = await local_search(
71	            local_config["search_url"],
72	            query,
73	            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
74	            proxy=local_config["proxy"],
75	        )
76	    elif backend == "google":
77	        from google_search_server import google_search
78	
79	        google_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["google"]
80	        result = await google_search(
81	            google_config["api_key"],
82	            query,
83	            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
84	            snippet_only=google_config["snippet_only"],
85	            proxy=google_config["proxy"],
86	        )
87	    else:
88	        raise ValueError(f"Unknown search backend: {backend}. " f"Must be either 'local' or 'google'.")
89	
90	    return _passages2string(result)

93	# IMPORTANT: When we need to collect log probabilities (logp), we CANNOT do any postprocessing
94	# on the strings returned from the inference engine (sglang). This is because:
95	# 1. We don't know how to truncate the corresponding tokens/logp arrays to match the modified string
96	# 2. Re-tokenizing the postprocessed string may produce different tokens than what the engine generated,
97	#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities
98	# Therefore, postprocess_responses is only used when return_logprob=False.
99	def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
100	    """
101	    Post-process response to ensure tag completeness.
102	    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
103	    """
104	    return (
105	        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
106	        if "</search>" in resp
107	        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
108	    )
109	
110	
111	def postprocess_predictions(prediction: str):
112	    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
113	    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
114	    if match:
115	        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
116	        action = match.group(1)
117	    else:
118	        content = ""
119	        action = None
120	
121	    return action, content
122	
123	
124	async def execute_predictions(prediction: str) -> str:
125	    action, content = postprocess_predictions(prediction)
126	
127	    if action == "search":
128	        search_query = content
129	        async with SEMAPHORE:
130	            search_results = await search(search_query)
131	        next_obs = f"\n\n<information>{search_results.strip()}</information>\n\n"
132	        done = False
133	    elif action == "answer":
134	        next_obs = ""
135	        done = True
136	    else:
137	        next_obs = "\nMy previous action is invalid. \
138	If I want to search, I should put the query between <search> and </search>. \
139	If I want to give the final answer, I should put the answer between <answer> and </answer>. Let me try again.\n"
140	        done = False
141	
142	    return next_obs, done

145	async def generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
146	    assert not args.partial_rollout, "Partial rollout is not supported for this function at the moment."
147	
148	    state = GenerateState(args)
149	
150	    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"
151	
152	    # Handle partial rollout samples: continue generation from existing response
153	    prompt_text = sample.prompt
154	    prompt_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
155	    sample.tokens = list(prompt_tokens_ids)
156	    sample.loss_mask = []
157	    response = ""
158	    response_token_ids = []
159	    loss_mask = []
160	    rollout_log_probs = [] if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] else None
161	    sample.rollout_top_p_token_ids = None
162	    sample.rollout_top_p_token_offsets = None
163	
164	    # BUGFIX: make the inference engine STOP at the tool/answer boundary.
165	    # Without a stop, sglang keeps emitting tokens after </search> / </answer>

167	    # via postprocess_responses when return_logprob=False; with return_logprob=True
168	    # (TIS) trimming is disabled to keep token/logp aligned, so the junk stayed in
169	    # the trajectory and got trained on (loss_mask=1) AND broke is_valid_sequence
170	    # (trailing content after </answer> -> format invalid -> lower reward).
171	    # Stopping at the tag avoids all of that and keeps token/logp aligned natively.
172	    # slime already sets no_stop_trim=True, so the closing tag is kept in the output.
173	    _stop_tags = ["</search>", "</answer>"]
174	    _existing_stop = sampling_params.get("stop") or []
175	    if isinstance(_existing_stop, str):
176	        _existing_stop = [_existing_stop]
177	    sampling_params = {**sampling_params, "stop": list(dict.fromkeys([*_existing_stop, *_stop_tags]))}
178	
179	    for _turn_idx in range(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["max_turns"]):
180	        payload = {
181	            "text": prompt_text + response,
182	            "sampling_params": sampling_params,
183	        }
184	        # Add log probability collection if enabled
185	        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
186	            payload["return_logprob"] = True
187	
188	        output = await post(url, payload)
189	
190	        # abort
191	        if output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"] == "abort":
192	            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
193	            return sample
194	
195	        cur_response = output["text"]
196	
197	        # Extract tokens and log probs based on configuration
198	        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
199	            # Extract log probs from output - required for TIS metrics
200	            if "output_token_logprobs" not in output["meta_info"]:
201	                raise RuntimeError(
202	                    "output_token_logprobs not found in output meta_info. "
203	                    "Make sure 'return_logprob': True is set in the payload."
204	                )
205	
206	            # Use token IDs and log probs directly from output_token_logprobs
207	            # This ensures perfect alignment between tokens and log probs
208	            # output_token_logprobs format: [[log_prob, token_id, ...], ...]
209	            cur_response_token_ids = [item[1] for item in output["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"]]
210	            cur_response_log_probs = [item[0] for item in output["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"]]
211	        else:
212	            # When not collecting log probs, we can safely postprocess the response
213	            cur_response = postprocess_responses(cur_response)
214	            # Tokenize the (possibly postprocessed) response
215	            cur_response_token_ids = state.tokenizer(cur_response, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
216	
217	        response += cur_response
218	        response_token_ids += cur_response_token_ids
219	        loss_mask += [1] * len(cur_response_token_ids)
220	        sample.append_response_tokens(
221	            args,
222	            tokens=cur_response_token_ids,
223	            log_probs=cur_response_log_probs if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] else None,
224	            trainable=True,
225	            meta_info=output["meta_info"] if "output_token_logprobs" in output["meta_info"] else None,
226	        )
227	
228	        # Add log probs if enabled
229	        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
230	            rollout_log_probs += cur_response_log_probs
231	
232	        if output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"] == "length":
233	            break
234	
235	        next_obs, done = await execute_predictions(cur_response)
236	        if done:
237	            break
238	
239	        assert next_obs != "", "Next observation should not be empty."
240	        obs_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(next_obs, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
241	        response += next_obs
242	        response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
243	        loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
244	        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)
245	
246	        # Add dummy log probs for observation tokens if enabled
247	        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
248	            rollout_log_probs += [0.0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
249	
250	            # Verify alignment when collecting log probs
251	            assert len(response_token_ids) == len(
252	                rollout_log_probs
253	            ), f"Token/logp length mismatch: {len(response_token_ids)} tokens vs {len(rollout_log_probs)} logps"
254	
255	    # Store statistics for wandb logging
256	    sample.tokens = prompt_tokens_ids + response_token_ids
257	    sample.response_length = len(response_token_ids)
258	    sample.response = response
259	    sample.loss_mask = loss_mask
260	    sample.prompt = prompt_text
261	
262	    # Store log probs if enabled
263	    if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
264	        sample.rollout_log_probs = rollout_log_probs if rollout_log_probs else None
265	
266	    match output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"]:
267	        case "length":
268	            sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
269	        case "abort":
270	            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
271	        case "stop":
272	            sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
273	
274	    return sample

277	async def reward_func(args, sample, **kwargs):
278	    """The reward function for retrieval-based question answering.
279	
280	    Args:
281	        args: the arguments
282	        sample: the sample to evaluate
283	    """
284	    if not isinstance(sample, Sample):
285	        raise TypeError("Sample must be an instance of Sample class.")
286	
287	    score = compute_score_em(
288	        solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
289	        ground_truth=sample.label["ground_truth"],
290	        format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"],
291	    )
292	
293	    return score

# Adapted from https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1/blob/ceee7b89655ed52f205b9beb98e1190c3eedcfb0/search_r1/llm_agent/generation.py
# This is a unified version supporting both local search and Google search, with optional log probability collection

import asyncio
import re

from qa_em_format import compute_score_em

from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

# Configuration for Search-R1
SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    # ============== General Configuration ==============
    "max_turns": 8,
    "topk": 3,
    "search_concurrency": 256,
    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"
    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
    "local": {
        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Google Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="google")
    "google": {
        "api_key": "your_api_key_here",  # Replace with your actual API key
        "snippet_only": True,  # Set to True to only return snippets
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Log Probability Collection ==============
    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities for TIS metrics
    # ============== Reward Model Configuration ==============
    "format_score": 0.2,
}


SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_concurrency"])


def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
    """
    Convert retrieval results to a formatted string.
    This function works with both google_search and local_search results.
    """
    format_reference = ""
    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
        title = content.split("\n")[0]
        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"

    return format_reference


async def search(query: str) -> str:
    """
    Perform search using either local search engine or Google search.
    The search backend is determined by SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"].
    """
    backend = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"]

    if backend == "local":
        from local_search_server import local_search

        local_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["local"]
        result = await local_search(
            local_config["search_url"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            proxy=local_config["proxy"],
        )
    elif backend == "google":
        from google_search_server import google_search

        google_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["google"]
        result = await google_search(
            google_config["api_key"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            snippet_only=google_config["snippet_only"],
            proxy=google_config["proxy"],
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown search backend: {backend}. " f"Must be either 'local' or 'google'.")

    return _passages2string(result)


# IMPORTANT: When we need to collect log probabilities (logp), we CANNOT do any postprocessing
# on the strings returned from the inference engine (sglang). This is because:
# 1. We don't know how to truncate the corresponding tokens/logp arrays to match the modified string
# 2. Re-tokenizing the postprocessed string may produce different tokens than what the engine generated,
#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities
# Therefore, postprocess_responses is only used when return_logprob=False.
def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
    """
    Post-process response to ensure tag completeness.
    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
    """
    return (
        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
        if "</search>" in resp
        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
    )


def postprocess_predictions(prediction: str):
    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
        action = match.group(1)
    else:
        content = ""
        action = None

    return action, content


async def execute_predictions(prediction: str) -> str:
    action, content = postprocess_predictions(prediction)

    if action == "search":
        search_query = content
        async with SEMAPHORE:
            search_results = await search(search_query)
        next_obs = f"\n\n<information>{search_results.strip()}</information>\n\n"
        done = False
    elif action == "answer":
        next_obs = ""
        done = True
    else:
        next_obs = "\nMy previous action is invalid. \
If I want to search, I should put the query between <search> and </search>. \
If I want to give the final answer, I should put the answer between <answer> and </answer>. Let me try again.\n"
        done = False

    return next_obs, done


async def generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
    assert not args.partial_rollout, "Partial rollout is not supported for this function at the moment."

    state = GenerateState(args)

    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    # Handle partial rollout samples: continue generation from existing response
    prompt_text = sample.prompt
    prompt_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    sample.tokens = list(prompt_tokens_ids)
    sample.loss_mask = []
    response = ""
    response_token_ids = []
    loss_mask = []
    rollout_log_probs = [] if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] else None
    sample.rollout_top_p_token_ids = None
    sample.rollout_top_p_token_offsets = None

    # BUGFIX: make the inference engine STOP at the tool/answer boundary.
    # Without a stop, sglang keeps emitting tokens after </search> / </answer>
    # (junk, even fabricated new "Question:"s). The example only trimmed that junk
    # via postprocess_responses when return_logprob=False; with return_logprob=True
    # (TIS) trimming is disabled to keep token/logp aligned, so the junk stayed in
    # the trajectory and got trained on (loss_mask=1) AND broke is_valid_sequence
    # (trailing content after </answer> -> format invalid -> lower reward).
    # Stopping at the tag avoids all of that and keeps token/logp aligned natively.
    # slime already sets no_stop_trim=True, so the closing tag is kept in the output.
    _stop_tags = ["</search>", "</answer>"]
    _existing_stop = sampling_params.get("stop") or []
    if isinstance(_existing_stop, str):
        _existing_stop = [_existing_stop]
    sampling_params = {**sampling_params, "stop": list(dict.fromkeys([*_existing_stop, *_stop_tags]))}

    for _turn_idx in range(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["max_turns"]):
        payload = {
            "text": prompt_text + response,
            "sampling_params": sampling_params,
        }
        # Add log probability collection if enabled
        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
            payload["return_logprob"] = True

        output = await post(url, payload)

        # abort
        if output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"] == "abort":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
            return sample

        cur_response = output["text"]

        # Extract tokens and log probs based on configuration
        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
            # Extract log probs from output - required for TIS metrics
            if "output_token_logprobs" not in output["meta_info"]:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "output_token_logprobs not found in output meta_info. "
                    "Make sure 'return_logprob': True is set in the payload."
                )

            # Use token IDs and log probs directly from output_token_logprobs
            # This ensures perfect alignment between tokens and log probs
            # output_token_logprobs format: [[log_prob, token_id, ...], ...]
            cur_response_token_ids = [item[1] for item in output["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"]]
            cur_response_log_probs = [item[0] for item in output["meta_info"]["output_token_logprobs"]]
        else:
            # When not collecting log probs, we can safely postprocess the response
            cur_response = postprocess_responses(cur_response)
            # Tokenize the (possibly postprocessed) response
            cur_response_token_ids = state.tokenizer(cur_response, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]

        response += cur_response
        response_token_ids += cur_response_token_ids
        loss_mask += [1] * len(cur_response_token_ids)
        sample.append_response_tokens(
            args,
            tokens=cur_response_token_ids,
            log_probs=cur_response_log_probs if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] else None,
            trainable=True,
            meta_info=output["meta_info"] if "output_token_logprobs" in output["meta_info"] else None,
        )

        # Add log probs if enabled
        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
            rollout_log_probs += cur_response_log_probs

        if output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"] == "length":
            break

        next_obs, done = await execute_predictions(cur_response)
        if done:
            break

        assert next_obs != "", "Next observation should not be empty."
        obs_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(next_obs, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
        response += next_obs
        response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
        loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)

        # Add dummy log probs for observation tokens if enabled
        if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
            rollout_log_probs += [0.0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)

            # Verify alignment when collecting log probs
            assert len(response_token_ids) == len(
                rollout_log_probs
            ), f"Token/logp length mismatch: {len(response_token_ids)} tokens vs {len(rollout_log_probs)} logps"

    # Store statistics for wandb logging
    sample.tokens = prompt_tokens_ids + response_token_ids
    sample.response_length = len(response_token_ids)
    sample.response = response
    sample.loss_mask = loss_mask
    sample.prompt = prompt_text

    # Store log probs if enabled
    if SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"]:
        sample.rollout_log_probs = rollout_log_probs if rollout_log_probs else None

    match output["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"]:
        case "length":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
        case "abort":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
        case "stop":
            sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED

    return sample


async def reward_func(args, sample, **kwargs):
    """The reward function for retrieval-based question answering.

    Args:
        args: the arguments
        sample: the sample to evaluate
    """
    if not isinstance(sample, Sample):
        raise TypeError("Sample must be an instance of Sample class.")

    score = compute_score_em(
        solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
        ground_truth=sample.label["ground_truth"],
        format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"],
    )

    return score

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prepare the inputs for the Search-R1 slime recipe:
#   1. the QA dataset  -> nq_hotpotqa_train/{train,test}.parquet
#   2. the retrieval corpus -> wiki-18 e5 FAISS index + wiki-18.jsonl
#
# It drives the data-preparation subset of the Search-R1 repo that ships next to
# this recipe (workspace/Search-R1). Nothing here trains a model.
#
# Usage:
#   bash prepare_data.sh                 # dataset + corpus
#   DATASET_ONLY=1 bash prepare_data.sh  # skip the ~130GB corpus download
#   CORPUS_ONLY=1  bash prepare_data.sh  # only the retrieval corpus
#
# Override any path via the environment variables below.
set -euo pipefail

# --- locations -------------------------------------------------------------
# Directory of this script (examples/search-r1), resolved so it works from any cwd.
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# The trimmed Search-R1 repo. Defaults to the copy staged in this workspace
# (workspace/Search-R1); at container runtime the recipe reads /root/Search-R1,
# so allow an override.
SEARCH_R1_DIR="${SEARCH_R1_DIR:-$(cd "$HERE/../../Search-R1" && pwd)}"

# Where prepared assets land. Keep them inside the repo's data/ dir so the paths
# match the recipe's --prompt-data (…/Search-R1/data/nq_hotpotqa_train/…).
DATA_DIR="${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}"
DATASET_DIR="${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}"
CORPUS_DIR="${CORPUS_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/wiki-18}"

# Which QA sources to merge. Train mixes NQ+HotpotQA (the recipe default); the
# test merge can span more sets for evaluation.
TRAIN_SOURCES="${TRAIN_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"
TEST_SOURCES="${TEST_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"

DATASET_ONLY="${DATASET_ONLY:-0}"
CORPUS_ONLY="${CORPUS_ONLY:-0}"
# Re-download even if the target files already exist.
FORCE="${FORCE:-0}"

if [[ ! -d "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process" ]]; then
  echo "error: Search-R1 data-prep scripts not found under: $SEARCH_R1_DIR" >&2
  echo "       set SEARCH_R1_DIR to the trimmed Search-R1 repo." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The merge scripts import verl.utils.hdfs_io from the repo root.
export PYTHONPATH="$SEARCH_R1_DIR${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

# --- 1) QA dataset ---------------------------------------------------------
prepare_dataset() {
  local train_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet"
  local test_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "==> QA parquet already present, skipping ($DATASET_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $train_parquet"
    echo "    -> $test_parquet"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Building QA parquet into $DATASET_DIR"
  echo "    train sources: $TRAIN_SOURCES"
  echo "    test  sources: $TEST_SOURCES"
  mkdir -p "$DATASET_DIR"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    train.parquet exists, skipping train merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TRAIN_SOURCES"
  fi

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    echo "    test.parquet exists, skipping test merge"
  else
    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py" \
      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TEST_SOURCES"
  fi

  echo "    -> $train_parquet"
  echo "    -> $test_parquet"
}

# --- 2) retrieval corpus (wiki-18 e5) --------------------------------------
prepare_corpus() {
  local index="$CORPUS_DIR/e5_Flat.index"
  local jsonl="$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl"

  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$index" && -f "$jsonl" ]]; then
    echo "==> wiki-18 corpus already present, skipping ($CORPUS_DIR)"
    echo "    -> $index"
    echo "    -> $jsonl"
    return
  fi

  echo "==> Downloading wiki-18 e5 index + corpus into $CORPUS_DIR"
  echo "    NOTE: the assembled index is ~130GB; ensure disk + bandwidth."
  mkdir -p "$CORPUS_DIR"

  # Pulls PeterJinGo/wiki-18-e5-index (part_aa, part_ab) and
  # PeterJinGo/wiki-18-corpus (wiki-18.jsonl.gz) from the HuggingFace Hub.
  python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/download.py" --save_path "$CORPUS_DIR"

  echo "    Assembling e5_Flat.index from shards"
  cat "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_* > "$index"
  rm -f "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_*

  if [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz" ]]; then
    echo "    Decompressing wiki-18.jsonl"
    gzip -df "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz"
  fi

  echo "    -> $index"
  echo "    -> $jsonl"
}

# --- run -------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$CORPUS_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_corpus
elif [[ "$DATASET_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
  prepare_dataset
else
  prepare_dataset
  prepare_corpus
fi

echo "==> Done."

11	@torch.compile(dynamic=True)
12	def compute_approx_kl(
13	    log_probs: torch.Tensor,
14	    log_probs_base: torch.Tensor,
15	    kl_loss_type: str,
16	    importance_ratio: torch.Tensor | None = None,
17	) -> torch.Tensor:
18	    """
19	    Compute the approximate KL divergence between two distributions.
20	    Schulman blog: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
21	
22	    Args:
23	        log_probs: Log probabilities of the new distribution.
24	        log_probs_base: Log probabilities of the base distribution.
25	        kl_loss_type: Type of KL estimator (k1, k2, k3, low_var_kl).
26	        importance_ratio: Optional IS ratio (π_θ/π_old) for unbiased KL estimation.
27	    """
28	    log_ratio = log_probs.float() - log_probs_base.float()
29	
30	    if kl_loss_type == "k1":
31	        kl = log_ratio
32	    elif kl_loss_type == "k2":
33	        kl = log_ratio**2 / 2.0
34	    elif kl_loss_type in ["k3", "low_var_kl"]:
35	        # The non negative kl approximation in
36	        # http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
37	        # Besides non negative, it is also unbiased and have lower variance.
38	        log_ratio = -log_ratio
39	        kl = log_ratio.exp() - 1 - log_ratio
40	    else:
41	        raise ValueError(f"Unknown kl_loss_type: {kl_loss_type}")
42	
43	    # Apply IS ratio for unbiased KL estimation (DeepSeek-V3.2)
44	    if importance_ratio is not None:
45	        kl = importance_ratio * kl
46	
47	    # Clamp only for low_var_kl for numerical stability
48	    if kl_loss_type == "low_var_kl":
49	        kl = torch.clamp(kl, min=-10, max=10)
50	
51	    return kl

54	def compute_opsm_mask(
55	    args: Namespace,
56	    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
57	    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
58	    advantages: list[torch.Tensor],
59	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
60	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
61	    """Compute Off-Policy Sequence Masking (OPSM) mask.
62	
63	    Args:
64	        args: Configuration containing `opsm_delta` threshold.
65	        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample.
66	        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample.
67	        advantages: Advantage values per sample.
68	        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.
69	
70	    Returns:
71	        Tuple of `(opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac)` where `opsm_mask` is a
72	        concatenated tensor of per-token masks and
73	        `opsm_clipfrac` is the count of masked sequences.
74	    """
75	    opsm_mask_list = []
76	    device = advantages[0].device
77	    opsm_clipfrac = torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
78	
79	    for full_log_prob, full_old_log_prob, advantage, loss_mask in zip(
80	        full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, advantages, loss_masks, strict=False
81	    ):
82	        # Calculate sequence-level KL
83	        seq_kl = ((full_old_log_prob - full_log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
84	
85	        # Create mask: 0 if (advantage < 0 and seq_kl > delta), else 1
86	        mask = ((advantage < 0) & (seq_kl > args.opsm_delta)).float()
87	        opsm_clipfrac += mask.sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
88	
89	        opsm_mask_list.append(1 - mask)
90	
91	    opsm_mask = torch.cat(opsm_mask_list, dim=0)
92	    return opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac

95	def compute_gspo_kl(
96	    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
97	    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
98	    local_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
99	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
100	) -> torch.Tensor:
101	    """Compute GSPO-style per-sequence KL divergence.
102	
103	    Args:
104	        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
105	        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
106	        local_log_probs: Local (CP-local) log-probs for expansion shape reference.
107	        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.
108	
109	    Returns:
110	        Concatenated tensor of per-token KL values where each token in a
111	        sequence has the same KL value (the sequence-level KL).
112	    """
113	    # Compute sequence-level KL and expand to per-token
114	    ppo_kl = [
115	        ((old_logprob - log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
116	        for log_prob, old_logprob, loss_mask in zip(full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, loss_masks, strict=False)
117	    ]
118	    ppo_kl = [kl.expand_as(log_prob) for kl, log_prob in zip(ppo_kl, local_log_probs, strict=False)]
119	    ppo_kl = torch.cat(ppo_kl, dim=0)

125	def compute_policy_loss(
126	    ppo_kl: torch.Tensor,
127	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
128	    eps_clip: float,
129	    eps_clip_high: float,
130	    eps_clip_c: float | None = None,
131	):
132	    ratio = (-ppo_kl).exp()
133	    pg_losses1 = -ratio * advantages
134	    pg_losses2 = -ratio.clamp(1 - eps_clip, 1 + eps_clip_high) * advantages
135	    clip_pg_losses1 = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2)
136	    clipfrac = torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float()

138	    if eps_clip_c is not None:

141	        ), f"The lower bound of the clip_ratio_c for dual-clip PPO should be greater than 1.0, but get the value: {eps_clip_c}."
142	        pg_losses3 = -eps_clip_c * advantages
143	        clip_pg_losses2 = torch.min(pg_losses3, clip_pg_losses1)
144	        pg_losses = torch.where(advantages < 0, clip_pg_losses2, clip_pg_losses1)

159	    """CISPO loss from MiniMax-M1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585, Eq. 4-5):

162	    Unlike PPO, the IS ratio is clipped under stop-gradient and the gradient flows

165	    disables the lower bound (``eps_clip >= 1.0``).

167	    ratio = (-ppo_kl).exp()
168	    ratio_truncated = torch.clamp(ratio, min=1.0 - eps_clip, max=1.0 + eps_clip_high)
169	    pg_losses = -ratio_truncated.detach() * advantages * log_probs
170	    clipfrac = (ratio_truncated != ratio).float()

371	def get_reinforce_plus_plus_returns(
372	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
373	    kl: list[torch.Tensor],
374	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
375	    response_lengths: list[int],
376	    total_lengths: list[int],
377	    kl_coef: float,
378	    gamma: float,
379	) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
380	    """
381	    Calculates discounted returns for REINFORCE++ (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03262)
382	
383	    Args:
384	        rewards (Tensor): A tensor of scalar rewards for each sequence.
385	        kl (List[Tensor]): List of per-token KL divergence tensors for sequence chunks.
386	        loss_masks (List[Tensor]): List of response-only loss masks for each full sequence.
387	        response_lengths (List[int]): The full length of each response sequence.
388	        total_lengths (List[int]): The full length of each sequence (prompt + response).
389	        kl_coef (float): Coefficient for the KL penalty.
390	        gamma (float): The discount factor.
391	
392	    Returns:
393	        List[torch.Tensor]: A list of return (G_t) tensors for the
394	                            local sequence chunks owned by the current GPU rank.
395	    """
396	    from megatron.core import mpu
397	
398	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
399	
400	    token_level_rewards = []
401	    for i in range(len(rewards)):
402	        local_kl_chunk = kl[i]
403	        total_len, response_len = total_lengths[i], response_lengths[i]
404	
405	        if cp_size > 1:
406	            # Step 1,2:Gather all chunks and token_offsets from all ranks and reconstruct the full response tensor by splitting and placing each part
407	            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import all_gather_with_cp
408	
409	            full_kl_response = all_gather_with_cp(local_kl_chunk, total_len, response_len)
410	        else:
411	            full_kl_response = local_kl_chunk
412	
413	        # Step 3: Compute returns on full response kl tensor.
414	        full_mask = loss_masks[i]
415	        assert full_mask.sum().item() > 0, f"Sequence at index {i} is fully masked."
416	        masked_kl = full_kl_response * full_mask
417	        rewards_for_seq = -kl_coef * masked_kl
418	        last_idx = full_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0][-1]
419	        rewards_for_seq[last_idx] += rewards[i]
420	        token_level_rewards.append(rewards_for_seq)
421	
422	    if not token_level_rewards:
423	        return []
424	
425	    max_len = max(rewards_for_seq.size(0) for rewards_for_seq in token_level_rewards)
426	    padded_rewards = token_level_rewards[0].new_zeros(len(token_level_rewards), max_len)
427	    for i, rewards_for_seq in enumerate(token_level_rewards):
428	        padded_rewards[i, : rewards_for_seq.size(0)] = rewards_for_seq
429	
430	    padded_returns = chunked_discounted_returns(padded_rewards, gamma)
431	
432	    final_returns_chunks = []
433	    for i, returns_for_seq in enumerate(padded_returns):
434	        returns_for_seq = returns_for_seq[: token_level_rewards[i].size(0)]
435	        if cp_size > 1:
436	            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import slice_log_prob_with_cp
437	
438	            total_len, response_len = total_lengths[i], response_lengths[i]
439	            local_returns_chunk = slice_log_prob_with_cp(returns_for_seq, total_len, response_len)
440	        else:
441	            local_returns_chunk = returns_for_seq
442	
443	        final_returns_chunks.append(local_returns_chunk)
444	
445	    return final_returns_chunks

448	def get_reinforce_plus_plus_baseline_advantages(
449	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
450	    kl: list[torch.Tensor],
451	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
452	    kl_coef: float,
453	) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
454	    """
455	    Calculates the unwhitened advantages for the REINFORCE++-baseline algorithm.
456	    Broadcasting the scalar (reward - group_baseline) to each token.
457	
458	    Args:
459	        rewards (Tensor): A tensor of scalar rewards, where the group-wise
460	                                baseline has already been subtracted.
461	        kl (list[Tensor]): A list of per-token KL divergence tensors. Used to

464	        kl_coef (float): Coefficient for the KL penalty.
465	
466	    Returns:
467	        list[Tensor]: A list of tensors containing the unwhitened advantages.
468	    """
469	    # Broadcast to get unwhitened advantages
470	    unwhitened_advantages = [
471	        torch.ones_like(kl_tensor) * reward_val - kl_coef * kl_tensor
472	        for kl_tensor, reward_val in zip(kl, rewards, strict=False)
473	    ]
474	
475	    return unwhitened_advantages

529	        # pad to max_len for batched GAE

534

547	        else:

553	            )
554	
555	        advantages_list = []
556	        returns_list = []
557	
558	        if cp_size > 1:
559	            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import slice_log_prob_with_cp
560	
561	            for total_len, resp_len, adv_row, ret_row in zip(
562	                total_lengths,
563	                response_lengths,
564	                full_advantages,
565	                full_returns,
566	                strict=False,
567	            ):
568	                adv_full = adv_row  # shape = [resp_len_i padded to max_len]
569	                ret_full = ret_row
570	
571	                adv_sliced = slice_log_prob_with_cp(adv_full[:resp_len], total_len, resp_len)
572	                ret_sliced = slice_log_prob_with_cp(ret_full[:resp_len], total_len, resp_len)
573	
574	                advantages_list.append(adv_sliced)

579	                L = response_lengths[i]

586	def vanilla_gae(
587	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
588	    values: torch.Tensor,
589	    gamma: float,
590	    lambd: float,
591	):
592	    B, T = rewards.shape
593	    device = rewards.device
594	    dtype = rewards.dtype
595	
596	    lastgaelam = torch.zeros(B, device=device, dtype=dtype)
597	    adv_rev = []
598	
599	    for t in reversed(range(T)):
600	        next_value = values[:, t + 1] if t < T - 1 else 0.0
601	        delta = rewards[:, t] + gamma * next_value - values[:, t]
602	        lastgaelam = delta + gamma * lambd * lastgaelam
603	        adv_rev.append(lastgaelam)
604	
605	    full_advantages = torch.stack(adv_rev[::-1], dim=1)  # [B, max_len]
606	    full_returns = full_advantages + values  # [B, max_len]
607	    return full_advantages, full_returns
